goal: DEPTH: sub-sections / config sections in real integration with the backend — raise real coverage and capability levels
must_build: AWS managed + customer managed keys lists/detail (General config, Key policy, Cryptographic configuration, Tags, Key rotation, Aliases), Create key wizard (symmetric/asymmetric/HMAC, usage, aliases, admins/users, policy review), Enable/Disable, Schedule/Cancel deletion

Backend: Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey/Sign/Verify/GenerateMac real in the core; key policy stored (not evaluated = limited); automatic rotation flag + rotation history; aliases CRUD; custom key stores = not_simulated

Liveness for the AWS managed key detail page: model AWS-managed keys being created on first use (e.g. Encrypt/GenerateDataKey with alias aws/<service> creates that key if missing, as AWS does when a service first uses it); the fixture triggers that with a unique service name and the page must show the new key
always: Every page wired to the native API on /_wire (no static data); liveness fixtures for every list/detail page
core/capabilities/aws/<service>.json: one entry per console section with honest level + probe; tests/conformance/test_capabilities.py must pass
Sections via <CapabilityContainer>; editable settings round-trip through native calls with saveNotice()
Registry 'offline' level = 'nano' level for now; the offline appliance is verified separately (CAP_BASE)
note:
DEPTH PASS (the base console is merged). Goal: turn this service's sub-sections and config sections into REAL backend integrations. For EACH capability entry listed in `depth_targets` decide:
  BUILD — Vyomi can model it in the shared core (state + native API semantics): implement it in core/<svc>_core.py (and the offline route if offline lacks it), add conformance checks in tests/conformance/, raise the entry's level in core/capabilities/<cloud>/<svc>.json (not_simulated→limited/full, config_only→limited/full where now ENFORCED, limited→full where a limitation is removed), wire the console section to it with a UI↔native-API round trip in consoles/tests/smoke-<cloud>.mjs and a "live" fixture for any list/detail page.

Prefer behaviour that is ENFORCED (e.g. lifecycle rules actually expire objects, a DLQ really receives, a policy really denies) over config that is only stored. House rules: keep consoles/src/<cloud>/kit/Capability.jsx as on base (add JSON imports only), list the service ONCE in registry.js, register any NEW core in wasm/build_cores.py + wasm/nano-boot.js (own line, never inside a // comment) + core/nano_registry.py + core/nano_persist.py (tests/conformance/test_nano_core_manifest.py), unique variable names in the smoke files, 'Vyomi' as plain text, re-vendor with python3 wasm/build_cores.py, rebuild bundles, COMMIT your source.

depth_targets.title: Key policy
limitations: The key policy document is stored and returned exactly as written, but Vyomi does not evaluate it — it never denies or allows a KMS call based on policy content.

depth_targets.title: Key rotation (automatic flag + on-demand)
limitations: Automatic rotation (EnableKeyRotation) is recorded with its period and reflected in GetKeyRotationStatus, but Vyomi has no background scheduler — it never fires on its own. Use on-demand rotation (RotateKeyOnDemand) to actually rotate the backing key material; ciphertext from before a rotation keeps decrypting, exactly like AWS.

depth_targets.title: Sign / Verify, GenerateMac / VerifyMac, Encapsulate / Decapsulate
limitations: Signatures, MACs and ML-KEM shared secrets are produced with Vyomi's own authenticated primitive (the same construction as Encrypt/Decrypt), not real RSA/ECC/ML-DSA math or ML-KEM lattice math. They are genuine, tamper-detected and key-separated, but only verifiable inside Vyomi — not with a real public key outside it.

depth_targets.title: Key administrators / key users / other AWS accounts pickers
limitations: The visual policy editor's IAM-principal pickers (key administrators, key users, other AWS accounts) aren't modeled; edit the key policy JSON directly in the Key policy tab, which is real.

depth_targets.title: Custom key stores (AWS CloudHSM / external key stores)
limitations: Creating, listing, updating and deleting a custom key store record is real and stateful. Connecting one is not: Vyomi has no real CloudHSM cluster or external XKS proxy to reach, so ConnectCustomKeyStore always ends in a FAILED connection state, same as AWS would report without reachable backing infrastructure. No key's material is ever stored in a custom key store.
